video_caption: The video segment opens with a close-up shot of a clear glass beaker containing a small amount of dark blue liquid at the bottom, resting on a dark surface. The beaker has measurement markings, including "100 ml" and "BORO 3.3," and a clear glass stirring rod is submerged in the blue liquid, extending vertically. Small bubbles are visible within the blue liquid. At 00:13, the scene transitions to a slightly wider view, showing the same beaker. A clear glass dropper, holding a vibrant red liquid, is positioned above the beaker, releasing a single drop into the blue solution. The red liquid appears to mix with the blue. The video then cuts to a black screen, where the word "Litmus:" is handwritten in white at the top left, with a small hand icon pointing to it.

The video opens with white handwritten text "Litmus: dye" on a black background. An image of a bowl of yellow curry with white rice, chicken, pineapple chunks, and red cherry tomatoes appears to the left. Next, an image of the back of a person's head with vibrant teal-blue hair tied in a messy bun appears in the center. Then, an image of several folded scarves or fabric pieces in shades of blue, teal, and green hanging on a rack appears to the right. All three images disappear, and the text "Lichens" is handwritten next to "Litmus: dye". A hand icon points to the word "Litmus" and then to "Lichens". Finally, a close-up image of light green, moss-like lichens growing on a dark brown tree branch, set against a blurry green background, appears below the text. The hand icon is briefly visible pointing to the lichens image.

The video segment opens with the text "Litmus: dye Lichens" displayed in white handwritten font at the top of a black screen, accompanied by an image of green lichen growing on a tree branch, suggesting the natural origin of litmus. The scene transitions to a black background with the yellow handwritten text "Acids taste Sour," which is then supplemented by images of lemons and oranges, demonstrating examples of sour, acidic foods. The text "Bases taste bitter" then appears in green, alongside images of bitter gourd and spinach, exemplifying bitter, basic foods. The narration emphasizes the danger of tasting unknown substances and introduces "Indicators" as a safe alternative. A hand icon points to the word "Indicators," which then branches into two categories: "Colour" and "Smell." The hand first points to "Colour," then to "Smell," as the narrator explains that indicators change either their color or smell. Finally, a list of specific indicators appears under each category: "Litmus" (highlighted in orange), "Turmeric," "Methyl Orange," and "Phenolphthalein" under "Colour," and "Vanilla," "Clove," and "Onion" under "Smell," with the narrator stating the focus of this video is on the Litmus indicator.

The video segment opens with a black screen displaying a handwritten mind map: "Indicators" at the top, branching into "Colour" and "Smell". Under "Colour", an arrow points to "Litmus". The screen then splits vertically, showing two brown glass bottles with "DIAGNOSTIC REAGENT" written on their labels. A pipette is shown inserting into the left bottle, which has a label "LITMUS BLUE SOLUTION", indicating it contains blue litmus solution. A blue rectangular box on the right of the screen states: "Blue litmus solution". Then, the right side of the screen reveals a second brown glass bottle, with a label "LITMUS RED SOLUTION", showing red litmus solution, and a pink rectangular box on the right labels it: "Red litmus solution". A thin yellow line separates the two halves of the screen. Following this, the left side displays a clear beaker containing a colorless liquid (an acid). A pipette is used to add blue litmus solution to this beaker, and the liquid slowly changes color from blue to red. Text appears on the black background to the right, stating "Acid" and "Blue → Red", summarizing the color change. Simultaneously, the right side of the screen shows another clear beaker with a colorless liquid (a base). A pipette adds red litmus solution to this beaker, and the liquid gradually turns blue. Text appears next to this action, stating "Base" and "Red → Blue", explaining the color change for litmus in a base. The video maintains this split screen, showing the acid beaker on the left with red liquid and the base beaker on the right with blue liquid.

The video displays two side-by-side experiments on a dark background, demonstrating the color changes of litmus in acids and bases. The left side, labeled "Acid," shows a dropper adding a blue liquid into a beaker containing a clear liquid, which turns red. A text overlay "Acid" is displayed above, and a green box highlights "Blue -> Red," indicating that blue litmus turns red in an acid. The right side, labeled "Base," shows a dropper adding a red liquid into a beaker with a clear liquid, which turns blue. Above it, the text "Base" is shown, with "Red -> Blue" indicating that red litmus turns blue in a base. The speaker explains the observed color change for acids, with the green highlight on "Blue -> Red" appearing at 0:05 to emphasize the point.

The video opens with a split screen, displaying two distinct sections. On the left, a glass dropper is seen dispensing a dark blue liquid, presumably blue litmus solution, into a clear glass beaker containing a reddish-pink solution. The beaker has visible measurement markings on its side. Above this section, the text "Acid" is displayed, followed by "Blue → Red" (with "Blue" written in blue and "Red" in red), indicating that acids turn blue litmus red. The right section of the screen is dark and appears to be a faded placeholder, showing only faint outlines of a beaker and a dropper. Above this section, the text "Base" is displayed, followed by "Red → Blue" (with "Red" written in red and "Blue" in blue), suggesting that bases turn red litmus blue. The narration poses a question about what would happen if red litmus were added to acid, and if a color change would occur, prompting the viewer to pause and consider the possibilities. The visual elements remain static as the narration continues, reinforcing the setup for the upcoming explanation.

The video opens with two small glass beakers, each containing a reddish-orange liquid, resting on a dark surface in front of a light-colored wall. Both beakers have visible measurement markings. The scene then briefly cuts to black before showing the same two beakers. Now, however, the reddish-orange liquid has been replaced by a clear, colorless liquid, presumably water, maintaining the same volume as before. The beakers and the background remain unchanged.

The segment begins with two clear glass beakers containing transparent liquid placed on a dark surface against a light-colored wall. A hand, holding a dropper filled with red liquid (litmus), adds the liquid to the first beaker, turning the solution reddish-pink. The narrator states that the color remains red, indicating no change. Next, the same hand, using a dropper filled with purple liquid (litmus), adds it to the second beaker, turning the solution purplish-blue. The narrator states that this color also remains unchanged. The scene then transitions to a black screen with white text that reads "Acids." Below this, "Blue -> Red" is written in blue and red font, and further to the right, "Red" is written in red. A hand-shaped cursor points at "Blue -> Red" and then at "Red." A yellow circle with a diagonal line (denoting "no change") appears around the "Red" text. Subsequently, "Bases" appears in white below "Acids." Below "Blue -> Red," new text appears: "Red -> Blue" in red and blue font. To the right, "Blue" appears in blue. The hand-shaped cursor points at "Red -> Blue" and then at "Blue." Finally, a yellow circle with a diagonal line appears around the "Blue" text on the right.

The video displays white text on a black background, outlining litmus paper reactions for different substances. On the top left, "Acids" is written, and next to it, "Blue -> Red" (blue text changing to pink/red) indicates the color change, accompanied by a red circle with a diagonal line through it, signifying no change from red. Below, "Bases" is shown, with "Red -> Blue" (pink/red text changing to blue) next to it, and a blue circle with a diagonal line, indicating no change from blue. A gray hand icon points to these descriptions. At 0:01, "Neutral" (initially gray, then white) appears below "Bases," followed by "No Colour change" (yellow text), and the hand icon points to it. From 0:13, two mnemonics appear on the right: "B2B" (gray, then white) and "B R B" (gray, then white, with 'R' becoming pink/red and the second 'B' becoming blue), explained by the hand icon pointing to "Bases turn Red to Blue." At 0:27, a question in pink/red, blue, and yellow text is displayed at the bottom: "On adding blue litmus to a solution, no colour change is observed. What can this solution be?" Below this, three gray options, "(a) Acid," "(b) Base," and "(c) Neutral," appear, each subsequently circled in yellow as they are mentioned. The hand icon highlights the question and the options.

The video segment features a black background displaying educational content about litmus tests. At the top left, under "Acids", the text "Blue -> Red" is shown, with a yellow circle around "Red" that has a red strike-through, and a yellow circle around "Blue". Below this, "Bases" is listed with "Red -> Blue", accompanied by a yellow circle around "Blue" with a blue strike-through, and a yellow circle around "Red". Further down, "Neutral" is described as having "No Colour change". On the top right, the text "B2B" (white) and "B R B" (pink) are visible. An orange question appears: "On adding blue litmus to a solution, no colour change is observed. What can this solution be ?". Three answer options are presented in black text with white circles: "(a) Acid", "(b) Base", and "(c) Neutral". A white cursor in the shape of a hand moves and highlights "No Colour change" under "Neutral" before placing a green checkmark next to option (c) "Neutral". The cursor then highlights "blue litmus" and "no colour change" in the question text. Subsequently, it places a green checkmark next to option (b) "Base". The cursor then highlights the "Bases" section, specifically "Red -> Blue" and the "Blue" circle, before returning to highlight the question and both options (b) and (c) with green checkmarks, indicating that both a base and a neutral solution would result in no color change when blue litmus is added.

The video segment opens with a question displayed on a black background, detailing litmus paper color changes: "Acids Blue -> Red", "Bases Red -> Blue", and "Neutral No Colour change". A hand icon interactively selects "Base" and then "Neutral" as possible answers to the question: "On adding blue litmus to a solution, no colour change is observed. What can this solution be?". Two mnemonics, "B2B" (Blue to Red) and "BRB" (Red to Blue), are also visible. The scene then transitions to two side-by-side images of hands holding small booklets of litmus paper: one showing reddish "Litmus Red" paper and the other showing purplish-blue "Blue Litmus" paper. This is followed by a demonstration in a lab setting, where a hand dips blue litmus paper into a clear solution in a beaker, and the submerged part immediately turns red, indicating an acidic solution. Next, the same hand dips red litmus paper into a clear solution in another beaker, and the submerged part turns blue, indicating a basic solution. The video concludes with a summary screen on a black background, showing "Litmus" at the center, surrounded by cloud-shaped labels: "Red", "Blue", "Indicator", and "Changes Colour". Below, placeholders for acid and base color changes are displayed ("Acid _ -> _", "Base _ -> _"), along with the "B2B" and "BRB" mnemonics, as a hand icon moves to highlight "Indicator" and then the mnemonics.
